To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the d = 4 and d = 5 Lorentz violating terms in the QCD Lagrangian are not independent, that the physical operator in the d = 6 operator basis is not gauge invariant, and that the physical operator does not mix back to and from the unphysical operator sector.
the physical d = 5 gauge-invariant operator does not mix to and between nuisance unphysical operators.

the d = 6 operator mixing matrix in the α gauge is not gauge invariant; the physical operator in d = 5 mixing has a gauge-invariant anomalous dimension eigenvalues; nuisance operators do not contribute to the physical sector; and the mixing of the physical operator to the unphysical operators is α-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the structure of the d=5 operator system in Q.C.D.? Is the physical operator gauge invariant? What are the anomalous dimensions of the operators? Are there mixing effects between the physical and unphysical operators?
the following topics: 1) the dimension-5 operator system in QED and in QCD, 2) dimension-5 Higgs-induced operators in nonleptonic decays, 3) the operator basis for nonleptonic decay in QCD.
the problem of calculating the renormalization group functions of the dimension-5 operator system in QED and QCD, and the mixing problem of the dimension-6 operator in QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is one physical gauge invariant operator and that it is the only gauge invariant operator in this system, and that the anomalous dimension eigenvalues of the physical operator are explicitly gauge invariant.
there is no d = 5 mixing problem.
there is one physical d = 5 gauge invariant operator and two unphysical operators which are not physical but which do mix among themselves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the physical d = 5 QCD operator mixes to and from the unphysical sector only through gauge-invariant Higgs-bosons and that the anomalous dimension eigenvalues for the physical operators are explicitly gauge invariant.
the d = 4 operator mixing problem is not a problem at all, but the d = 6 operator mixing problem is.
the d = 6 operator system in QED is more complicated, but the d = 7 operator system is simpler.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the d = 6 operator mixing problem in α can be reduced to an analogous problem in the d = 4 theory.
the physical operator is the only gauge-invariant operator that mixes with other operators in the d = 6 operator system, and the mixing is explicitly gauge invariant.
the gauge invariance of the physical sector is a very robust property of operator mixing.
